blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 21 in June to 15 in September (−28.6%), and it took 43.2% of the city’s 37 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 34 in June to 32 in September (−5.9%), and it took 44.6% of the city’s 56 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Central Meadows for detached houses in August, September (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in June (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, September (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Central Meadows
Solaris at Meadows Gate — 12069 Harris Road

(part of the complex is also addressed 12079 Harris Road). Built 2010, 144 units (building directory, secondary source). The directory records restrictions as: pets not allowed, rentals allowed. Current listings call it "Pitt Meadows' only concrete high-rise" and "the only concrete and steel building" in the city — that is listing language, attributed here as a listing claim, not an independently verified city-wide fact; a current unit listing independently records pets as "No Cats" at unit level, consistent with the directory's no-pets line. Directory amenities: bike room, elevator, in-suite laundry.
Origin — 11950 Harris Road

Built 2008, 4 storeys, per current listings, which board-classify the building in Central Meadows; one listing records construction as frame wood with brick exterior and vinyl siding, and current listings describe a clubhouse/amenity room with a full kitchen and a secure bike room. Pet position is listing-level only: listings show cats OK, and current listings state "1 dog or 2 cats permitted" — a verified building bylaw summary is UNCONFIRMED. One listing notes a new roof and gutters in 2023. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Streets, schools and getting around Central Meadows

items.t: Central Meadows is a City of Pitt Meadows board sub-area. The City does not publish an official neighbourhood boundary or name for it — the closest official planning name is the OCP Municipal Town Centre, covering the Harris Road corridor, the North Lougheed Area and the Civic Centre, with Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) at the north edge, the Canadian Pacific (CPKC) rail line along Hammond Road, and Harris Road as the main street. City Hall is at 12007 Harris Road.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the Harris Road corridor in the Town Centre — Solaris at Meadows Gate and Origin both stand on Harris Road — plus the Advent Road pocket at the area's south-west side, which current listings board-classify as Central Meadows (Meadowland Village townhomes and the Meadowlands housing co-operative).
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Pitt Meadows condos & townhomes median was $662,500 in September 2026 ($566/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 40 days on market).

Transit anchors: Pitt Meadows Station, on Harris Road in the urban core, gives West Coast Express service to Waterfront Station, Vancouver, Monday to Friday in peak periods — the City states the trip to downtown Vancouver is about 45 minutes. Buses include route 701 (Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place / Maple Ridge East, via Harris Road and Hammond Road), route 791 (Haney Place to Braid Station), the 719/722 Meadowtown–Fraser Way circular service, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus stop at Harris Road on Lougheed Highway.

Civic anchors on the corridor: Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre at 12027 Harris Road, Pitt Meadows Public Library at 200-12099 Harris Road, sxwhekwnes (Spirit Square) at 11985 Harris Road, and Meadowtown Shopping Centre at 19800 Lougheed Highway at the area's north-east edge.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Central Meadows

items.t: Short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows: A City staff report states: "Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in Zoning Bylaw" — the use itself is banned city-wide, so an STR bylaw question never arises here. Pitt Meadows also appears in the Province's principal-residence-requirement community list for short-term rentals.

Floodplain is the city's defining land rule: the City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of the Pitt Meadows land base lies within the Fraser River and Pitt River floodplain (an older City figure of approximately 86% is superseded — do not use it), and the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes. Central Meadows is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) of the Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District.

Pitt Meadows property taxes and drainage levy: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026 under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), with a 5% penalty added after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026. The same bylaw carries a separate drainage levy — for 2026 the residential (Class 1) drainage rate is $0.1082 per $1,000 of taxable value, alongside the general municipal rate of $2.8438 per $1,000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Meadows

items.t: The floodplain number changed between City documents. The City's 2020 Business Plan says over 95% of Pitt Meadows is floodplain; an earlier OCP-era figure of roughly 86% still circulates in secondary sources. Use "over 95%" and cite the Business Plan.

Solaris carries two civic addresses. The directory address is 12069 Harris Road, but part of the complex is addressed 12079 Harris Road — when ordering strata documents or checking a tax record, confirm which address the specific unit carries.

The Advent Road pocket mixes three tenures on one street. Meadowland Village (freehold strata townhomes, 55+), Meadowlands Housing Co-operative (55+ co-op membership housing) and detached houses all sit on or off Advent Road, and current listings board-classify the pocket as Central Meadows even though it reads as a quiet residential street rather than Town Centre. A search that treats every Advent Road "unit" as a strata condo will misprice the co-op and the townhomes alike.

The Harris Road rail crossing is being rebuilt under the condos' street. The Pitt Meadows Road and Rail Improvements Project includes a new four-lane underpass below the CPKC main rail crossing at Harris Road, with work on the Kennedy Road overpass paused and priority given to the Harris Road underpass — directly relevant to Harris Road traffic past Solaris and Origin during construction.

A 1,215 m² figure in City material is a subdivision minimum, not a development minimum. The City's SSMUH update clarifies the 1,215 sq m figure in Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011 is a minimum lot area for subdivision in the R-3/R-4/R-6 zones and does not apply to development on existing lots — quoting it as a multi-family site minimum misstates the rules.
The North Lougheed corridor is the city's next growth area.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Meadows
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Town Centre house lots: detached houses on the residential streets under RS Large Lot Residential, R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential zones in Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011, with multi-family buildings concentrated on Harris Road, where the OCP designates high and medium density multifamily and mixed-use commercial/residential development.
Lot character from the zones, as the bylaw states it: These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

The 1,215 m² clarification that changes lot math: the 1,215 m² figure is a subdivision minimum ONLY — the City's SSMUH implementation update clarifies it does not apply to development on existing lots, so an existing smaller Town Centre lot can still be developed under R-3 / R-4 / R-6.

ALR vs non-ALR, as documented: the City's 2020 Business Plan states 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the ALR and agriculture remains the predominant land use citywide. ALR parcels inside the Town Centre core: per-address check only (research UNVERIFIED item) — no Town Centre ALR split is stated.

Servicing: the research documents the diked, drained urban context (drainage Area 3 — Kennedy, including McKechnie — the urban development area serviced by ditches, culverts and storm sewers, discharging to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers) and a separate drainage levy. A parcel-level municipal water/sewer vs well/septic statement: UNCONFIRMED in the research — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

Flood position: over 95% of the city land base is in the Fraser / Pitt floodplain behind 60 km of dikes (City 2020 Business Plan — the governing figure in these notes; the live-page "over 85%" conflict is flagged at the top and).

Market context, labelled correctly: Pitt Meadows IS a SnapStats-covered community. SnapStats has NO land category — neither figure is a land figure, sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only), and no detached figure is presented as a land figure.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Meadows

items.t: Central Meadows is the Town Centre part of the City of Pitt Meadows, BC, in Metro Vancouver, on the traditional territory of q̓ic̓əy̓ (Katzie) First Nation; City Hall is at 12007 Harris Road.

Working geography from the Town Centre description: Harris Road as the main street (north–south), Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) at the north edge, and the Canadian Pacific (CPKC) rail line along Hammond Road. Nearby: Mid Meadows to the south-east, West Meadows to the west, North Meadows across Lougheed Highway to the north, and Maple Ridge to the east.

Transit and commute: Pitt Meadows Station, on Harris Road in the urban core, gives West Coast Express service to Waterfront Station, Vancouver, Monday to Friday in peak periods — the City states the trip to downtown Vancouver is about 45 minutes; buses include route 701, route 791, the 719/722 circular service, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus stop at Harris Road. Golden Ears Way / Golden Ears Bridge to the east serves travel toward Langley and Surrey. Driving commute times: UNVERIFIED.

Civic core: Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre, 12027 Harris Road; Pitt Meadows Public Library, 200-12099 Harris Road (the city's only FVRL branch); sxwhekwnes (Spirit Square), 11985 Harris Road; Harris Road Park by Lougheed Highway. Shopping: Meadowvale Shopping Centre (Save-On-Foods, per the City's Commercial & Industrial Lands Analysis) in the Harris Road North commercial area, and Meadowtown Shopping Centre, 19800 Lougheed Highway (Real Canadian Superstore), at the north-east edge. Nearest hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.

Schools: SD42 catchments are address-based and SD42 has no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. Both schools are physically in the area — Pitt Meadows Elementary, 11941 Harris Road, and Pitt Meadows Secondary, 19438 116B Avenue, the only public secondary school in Pitt Meadows. That sample result does not transfer to other addresses.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Meadows

items.t: Suites: one secondary suite per principal dwelling unit, 33 to 90 m², inside the same building, where the zone permits it; garden suites one per lot at 33 to 90 m² in the zones listed in the City garden suite guide, including RS — and a lot with a garden suite cannot also have a secondary suite.
Floodplain — the defining lot rule: LIVE CONFLICT: all five Pitt Meadows guide pages state "over 85%" (City Financial Plan 2026–2030 attribution) — flagged at the top, never silently resolved.

Property taxes and drainage levy: under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), Class 1 Residential rates per $1,000 are $2.8438 general municipal and $0.1082 drainage levy; taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026. The drainage levy is a holding cost on every lot in this diked city. A 2026 flat utility fee amount: UNVERIFIED in the research.

Heritage diligence (Harris Road lots): Harris Road heritage buildings are on the City heritage register, including the Pitt Meadows General Store and Post Office at 12294 Harris Road, now the Pitt Meadows Museum — heritage status is a title-level check on older Harris Road lots.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Meadows

items.t: The City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% floodplain; the superseded OCP Bylaw 2352, 2007 era put it at about 86%, and all five Pitt Meadows guide pages now state "over 85%" sourced to the City Financial Plan 2026–2030.

The Harris Road rail crossing is being grade-separated. The Pitt Meadows Road and Rail Improvements Project includes a new four-lane underpass below the CPKC main rail crossing at Harris Road, with work on the Kennedy Road overpass paused and priority given to the Harris Road underpass — the corridor most Town Centre lots front or feed into.

78% farmland is why Town Centre lots carry the density. With 78% of the city land base in the ALR, new supply is corridor infill and SSMUH on existing urban lots, not new bare-land subdivisions — the scarcity is structural.

items.t: Municipality: City of Pitt Meadows, BC, in Metro Vancouver, on the traditional territory of q̓ic̓əy̓ (Katzie) First Nation; City Hall is at 12007 Harris Road.

Boundaries: no official street-by-street boundary is published. The Town Centre description covers the Harris Road corridor and the North Lougheed Area, with Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) at the north edge, the Canadian Pacific (CPKC) rail line along Hammond Road, and Harris Road as the main street. Nearby areas: Mid Meadows to the south-east, West Meadows to the west, North Meadows across Lougheed Highway to the north, and the City of Maple Ridge to the east.

Transit: Pitt Meadows Station, on Harris Road in the urban core, gives West Coast Express service to Waterfront Station, Vancouver, Monday to Friday in peak periods, and bus connections including route 701, route 791, the 719/722 Meadowtown–Fraser Way circular service, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus stop at Harris Road.

Parks, recreation and library: sxwhekwnes (Spirit Square), 11985 Harris Road, sits in the civic centre near City Hall; Harris Road Park by Lougheed Highway serves the north end; Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre is at 12027 Harris Road; Pitt Meadows Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 200-12099 Harris Road, is the city's only FVRL branch.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Central Meadows
Verified community inside Central Meadows: 1 — Meadow Highlands Mobile Home Co-operative, co-operative tenure form.
The parks and communities

items.t: Membership approval is a closing condition, per the co-op itself: to become a member you must purchase a mobile home occupying one of the 162 pads, and once a purchase has been tentatively agreed the purchaser must be approved for membership by first meeting with the Board of Directors — that meeting takes place prior to closing and is a condition that must be included in all purchase agreements. Build that approval step into subject dates; it is the co-op equivalent of (and a different process from) a pad park's RTB Form 10 assignment consent in.

Age position — affirmatively NOT 55+: NO source checked states any age restriction for Meadow Highlands, and the record points the other way — the co-op's own site names a play area among the amenities the Pad Assessments maintain, and listings advertise an "outdoor kids play area" and proximity to schools. It is a family/all-age co-op park, NOT a 55+ park, despite appearing in seniors resource directories and despite being the Pitt Meadows property most likely to be assumed seniors housing.

Zoning story: Meadow Highlands' land use was governed by a land use contract that expired June 30, 2024 (as mandated by the Province) over an underlying RM-1 Multi-Family Residential zone that does not permit manufactured homes; the City's Zoning Amendment Bylaw 2991, 2024 rezoned the property to a new Residential Mobile Home (RMH) zone to match the existing use.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Meadows

items.t: The working frame used by the City's Town Centre description: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) at the north edge, the Canadian Pacific (CPKC) rail line along Hammond Road, and Harris Road as the main street.

Nearby areas: Mid Meadows (Bonson Road / Osprey Village) to the south-east, West Meadows (airport and farm lands) to the west, North Meadows across Lougheed Highway to the north, and the City of Maple Ridge to the east.

Where the mobile-home stock sits: Meadow Highlands is on Ponderosa Blvd off Hammond Road, at the south edge of the Town Centre frame — park addresses also run on Pinyon Lane, Planetree Lane and Poplar Drive.
It is family townhome product, not a manufactured-home park in any source.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect park-home buyers in Central Meadows

items.t: Zoning / OCP — Pitt Meadows frame: Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011 governs: houses sit under RS Large Lot Residential and R-3 / R-4 / R-6 Urban Residential zones (R-3 up to 3 units per lot, R-4 up to 4, R-6 up to five units, or six where at least one unit meets the adaptable housing requirements in the BC Building Code on lots close to frequent transit; the 1,215 sq m minimum lot area in those zones is a subdivision minimum only). OCP: "I See Pitt Meadows 2040," Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 2864, 2020, adopted September 27, 2022 — the Municipal Town Centre designation covers this area. Bylaw No. 2505, 2011 - Consolidated Version_0.pdf

Floodplain: The city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes; Central Meadows is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie). Floodplain Designation and Construction Control Bylaw No. 2384, 2008 sets the Flood Construction Level (FCL) as the Designated Flood Level plus a freeboard of 0.6 metres — and for a manufactured home, the ground level or top of a pad must be no lower than that elevation.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Meadows

items.t: Meadow Highlands ran on an expiring land use contract until 2024: The park's land use was governed by a provincially-mandated-to-expire land use contract (expired June 30, 2024) over an RM-1 zone that does not permit manufactured homes; Zoning Amendment Bylaw 2991, 2024 created a Residential Mobile Home (RMH) zone for it.

Three "Meadow-" names, three tenures, one pocket: Meadowland Village (18960 Advent Rd) is the 55+ strata you can buy; Meadowlands Housing Co-operative (19032 Advent Rd) is the 55+ co-op you join; Meadow Highlands (Hammond Road) is the all-age manufactured-home co-op. Verify the tenure from the address, not the name.

faq.q: What sold in Central Meadows in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached recorded 15 active listings and 4 sold (27% sales ratio), and Condos & Townhomes recorded 32 active listings and 5 sold (16%) — the largest inventory of any Pitt Meadows sub-area that month. At the Pitt Meadows community level — NOT Central Meadows' figures — the detached median sale price was $1,160,000 and the Condos & Townhomes median was $662,500 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Can I run a short-term rental or add a suite in Central Meadows?
faq.a: Short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows — short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in the Zoning Bylaw. A secondary suite is a different question: one suite per principal dwelling unit at 33 to 90 sq m inside the same building where the zone permits it, or one garden suite per lot in the zones listed in the City guide — never both on one lot.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Central Meadows Pitt Meadows than in June?
faq.a: In Central Meadows Pitt Meadows, listings of houses fell from 21 in June to 15 in September (−28.6%); condos and townhomes fell from 34 in June to 32 in September (−5.9%).

faq.q: How big is Central Meadows Pitt Meadows compared with the rest of Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: In September 2026, Central Meadows Pitt Meadows held 40.5% of the 37 houses listed in Pitt Meadows and 48.5% of the 66 condos and townhomes listed in Pitt Meadows.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Central Meadows Pitt Meadows from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 16 houses and 25 condos and townhomes sold in Central Meadows Pitt Meadows over those 4 months.

faq.q: Can I run an Airbnb in a Central Meadows condo?
faq.a: No. Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use under Pitt Meadows' Zoning Bylaw at all, and the Province's principal-residence requirement also lists Pitt Meadows. Long-term rental of a strata unit is a separate question — strata rental bylaws are void since November 24, 2022.

faq.q: Is Solaris really the city's only concrete tower?
faq.a: Current listings describe Solaris at Meadows Gate (12069 Harris Road, built 2010, 144 units per the building directory) as "Pitt Meadows' only concrete high rise." That is listing language; the verified facts from the directory are the year, the unit count and the restriction set (pets not allowed, rentals allowed).

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the Harris Road buildings?
faq.a: It differs by building: the directory records Solaris as pets not allowed (and a current unit listing records "No Cats"), while Origin listings state "1 dog or 2 cats permitted" with cats OK. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC, so the registered bylaws on the Form B govern — Origin's position is listing-level only and a verified bylaw summary is UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: Is Meadowland Village a condo complex?
faq.a: No — it is a townhouse/rancher strata at 18960 Advent Road (built 1988, freehold strata), board-classified Central Meadows, with a published 55+ age restriction and pets allowed with restrictions in current listings.

faq.q: And the Meadowlands building on Advent Road — can I buy a unit there?
faq.a: Not as a strata purchase. Meadowlands Housing Co-operative (19032 Advent Road) is a 55+ housing co-operative listed by CHF BC — occupancy is by co-op membership, there is no strata lot to buy in the ordinary way and no Form B.

faq.q: What townhouses can I actually buy in Central Meadows?
faq.a: Townhouse-form units also trade at 12188 Harris Road, but that complex's name is UNCONFIRMED in public sources.

faq.q: Is Meadowland Village 20 homes or 26?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: Is the Advent Road building beside Meadowland Village the same thing?
faq.a: No. Meadowlands Housing Co-operative (19032 Advent Road) is a 55+ co-op — occupancy is by membership, there is no strata lot to buy and no Form B. Meadowland Village is the strata purchase; the co-op is excluded from the count for exactly that reason.

faq.q: Is there acreage to buy in Central Meadows?
faq.a: Not as a product. This is the city's urban Town Centre — fee-simple house lots under RS / R-3 / R-4 / R-6 (subdivision minimums 0.2 ha in RS and 1,215 sq m in R-3/R-4/R-6) with multifamily on Harris Road. The city's farm acreage is in West Meadows, not here.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a Town Centre lot, and what servicing applies?
faq.a: Confirm the works required with the City for the specific lot.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Central Meadows address?
faq.a: SD42 has no middle tier and catchments are address-based, so confirm every other address in the locator.

faq.q: Is Central Meadows in a floodplain?
faq.a: Confirm floodplain, dike and drainage details for the specific lot with the City.

faq.q: What mobile-home buying actually exists in Central Meadows?
faq.a: One community: Meadow Highlands Mobile Home Co-operative on Ponderosa Blvd / Hammond Road — a co-operative manufactured-home park of 162 homes where members hold shares in the co-op that collectively owns the land. There is no verified pad-rental park in Central Meadows.

faq.q: In the co-op, do I own the land?
faq.a: Not individually. The property — all 162 pads, roads, hall, pool, office, RV parking and infrastructure — is owned collectively by the 162 members; you purchase shares in the co-op and pay a monthly Pad Assessment based on your pad's size. That is neither a fee-simple lot nor a rented pad, and the co-op's membership and occupancy documents govern.

faq.q: Is Meadow Highlands a 55+ park?
faq.a: No — affirmatively not. No source states any age restriction, the co-op maintains a kids' play area, and listings advertise that play area and school proximity. It is a family/all-age co-op park. Do not confuse it with the Meadowlands Housing Co-operative on Advent Road, which IS 55+ — but is built row-homes, not a manufactured-home park.

faq.q: Does the co-op have to approve me as a buyer?
faq.a: Yes — on the co-op's own terms: once a purchase is tentatively agreed, the purchaser must be approved for membership by meeting with the Board of Directors before closing, and that meeting is a condition that must be included in all purchase agreements. That is a different process from a rental park's RTB Form 10 assignment consent.
